candidate.educational_objective: Use time, distance, shielding, and facility radiation-safety instructions to minimize occupational exposure while providing necessary care to a hospitalized brachytherapy patient.

options.A: Remain close to the radiation source because increasing distance does not meaningfully reduce exposure.
options.B: Rely on routine gloves and an isolation gown as equivalent substitutes for radiation shielding.
options.C: Withhold all necessary nursing care until the radioactive source is removed.
options.D: Minimize time near the source, maximize distance when care permits, and follow the prescribed shielding and radiation-safety procedures.

candidate.rationale: The NRC identifies time, distance, and shielding as core radiation-protection principles: reducing time lowers dose, increasing distance lowers intensity and dose, and proper shielding reduces penetrating radiation exposure. NRC regulation 10 CFR §35.410 also requires radiation-safety instruction for personnel caring for certain hospitalized brachytherapy patients, including safe handling and shielding instructions. Necessary care should be provided using these controls rather than relying on routine barrier PPE or avoiding care.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Occupational radiation exposure is minimized by limiting time, increasing distance, and using appropriate shielding; personnel caring for specified hospitalized brachytherapy patients require safe-handling and shielding instruction.
